title: Find the Area of Figures

sourceTextSkillAdaptation.prompt: Find the area of the T-shaped Figure 2 shown above. Count the equal unit intervals to infer its rectangle side lengths, split it without overlap, and enter the area with square units. Explain your reasoning.

originalSourceHeadings.heading: Warm-up: Number Talk: Extend Make a Ten (10 minutes)
Activity 2: How Many Pavers Do We Need? (15 minutes)

originalSourceVisualAltDescriptions: T-shaped figure. If split horizontally, 2 rectangles. Top, 8 tick marks by 3 tick marks. Bottom, 4 tick marks by 2 tick marks.
6-sided shape. Straight sides. All side lengths meet at right angles. Bottom, 3 ft. Right side rises 2 ft, then goes right 6 ft, up 4 ft. Top side length, 9 ft. Left side length, 6 ft.
Photograph of patio. Floor paved with square tiles.

learnerSourceCheck.prompt: Find the area of the T-shaped Figure 2 shown above. Count the equal unit intervals to infer its rectangle side lengths, split it without overlap, and enter the area with square units. Explain your reasoning.

supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.sourceGoal: Let’s find the area of figures.
supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.sourceLearningGoals: Calculate the area of ungridded figures made of rectangles using multiplication and addition.
teachingSteps: Use make-ten or place-value reasoning for113,123,243,253.
Ask what information is missing from an outline with no unit or lengths.
Infer side lengths from partial grid squares and boundary intervals; multiply non-overlapping rectangle areas.
Find Noah’s 42-paver count and42 ft² area using two splits.
Make and compare labelled displays, then solve the distinct ungridded Cool-down.
supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.caution: Do not confuse the44-square partial figure,32-square T-shape and42-ft² patio. Count intervals, exclude overlaps, and distinguish counts from square units.

firstPartyPractice.prompt: A separate first-party patio is made from two non-overlapping rectangles:8 ft by3 ft and4 ft by2 ft. How many pavers covering 1 ft² each are needed? Enter the count. Draw the parts and explain; this is a different patio from Noah’s.

independentEdulyticsCoolDown.prompt: New Edulytics ungridded figure: use the separately labelled Cool-down model above. Find its area, including square units. Show a non-overlapping decomposition and a matching expression, then explain another split.

stageC.humanRubric: Opening outline has no determined numerical area until a unit/measurements are supplied. Figure 1 has area44 square units; Figure 2 T-shape has32. Count intervals rather than short marks. Noah’s different patio requires42 one-ft² pavers and has42 ft² area, using 36+6 or18+24. Review inferred side lengths, non-overlap, labelled display, measurement choices, explanation and actual MLR7 partner/group comparison. Numeric results do not certify these tasks.

matchingScope: Distinct partial44-square, T32-square and Noah42-paver/42-ft² contracts; counts and unit-labelled areas separated. No determined numerical area for opening unlabelled outline. Inference/explanation/display/interaction require teacher review.
